absent: Full field layout of the session state type beyond the observed longterm page array, count and mutex.
Semantics of get, pin and unpin acquisition primitives, their flag values and their release counterparts.
Behavior of DMA pin verification, page dumping and page release helpers used by the benchmark loop.
Window base, size, index and address translation formulas, protection value and hash sizing for persistent mapping.
Maximum local nesting depth, fixed slot bounds and architecture-specific overrides for local hooks.
Address space lock, file and inode handling, debug filesystem creation and user copy failure details.

Wait queue, sleep and wakeup ordering plus interrupt control inside locking primitives.

findings.text: A debug test node supports open, ioctl and release. Open allocates zeroed session state, marks the file nonseekable and initializes a mutex for longterm work before attaching the state to the file. Release stops any active longterm pin, destroys the mutex, clears the file pointer and frees the session. Ioctl first separates benchmark and dump requests from longterm start, stop and read requests, rejecting unknown numbers.

Benchmark ioctls exchange a descriptor with user space, execute a timed acquisition loop over a user range, verify pinned state without affecting timing, optionally dump selected pages, then time the release phase and report both durations plus the amount actually processed. Longterm ioctls instead start a persistent pin, stop it, or copy pinned contents out through a temporary per-page mapping.

The dossier provides durable high memory mapping with reference counting, a non-creating lookup that bumps the count only when a mapping already exists, an unmapping operation, bidirectional translation between pages and virtual addresses, reverse lookup from virtual address to page, global flush of unused entries, and counters for free and total high memory.

The dossier provides thread-local temporary mapping keyed by page or frame number with caller supplied protection, plus indexed unmapping. Low memory pages can return their direct address without creating a mapping, while high memory pages install a fixed slot entry. Slot table lookup either queries by virtual address in non-linear builds or reuses a cached base offset by slot index. Unmapping clears the slot and balances migration and preemption controls.

Additional services include zeroing of up to two byte ranges that may span multiple subpages of a compound page with per-subpage temporary mapping and cache maintenance, and helpers that sum free or managed pages across populated high memory zones.

The main test descriptor carries two durations for acquisition and release, a user address and byte length, a per-call page limit, two flag words for acquisition options and test options, and a small fixed-size selection table where each nonzero slot holds a one-based page index relative to the base and zero means no action.

The longterm descriptor carries a user address and byte length plus a flag word selecting write access and fast acquisition. The separate read request passes only a destination user address where pinned contents should be copied.

Persistent mapping state consists of a fixed-size count array indexed by slot number, a cacheline aligned central spin lock, and a page table base for the reserved window. Temporary mapping state consists of a per-thread nesting depth and a saved protection array indexed by nesting level, plus a cached page table pointer for fixed slots.

A slot count of zero means free and reusable. A count of one means free but still mapped and requiring a flush before reuse. Larger counts mean actively mapped. Global flush only clears slots at one, resetting them to zero, clearing their table entries, detaching their page associations and issuing a single range flush when any slot changed.

Benchmark requests reject addresses or sizes outside the unsigned long range and reject ranges whose end overflows. The page count derives from size divided by page size. Fast variants skip the address space read lock while all other benchmark variants hold it killably across the loop. Longterm start additionally requires page aligned address and size, a positive page count and no preexisting active pin.

Color selection always yields zero, slot scanning advances a static round-robin counter masked to the window size, wraparound is detected only at slot zero, the available entry count always equals the full window size, and all waiters share one static wait queue. Together these define a single-color configuration with no per-color partitioning.

The per-thread nesting depth advances by a build-dependent step and must stay within a fixed maximum and never go negative. The hardware slot derives from the logical position plus a multiple of the maximum by the current processor number, giving each processor a disjoint window. Mapping and unmapping use the same derivation.

Low memory pages resolve directly without consulting mapping tables. High memory pages resolve through a hashed bucket list keyed by page identity. Adding an association links a preassigned slot object for the virtual address, while removal scans the bucket for the matching page and unlinks it. Reverse lookup checks the persistent window first, then the current thread local slots, then falls back to direct conversion.

Zeroing first validates both ends against the compound page size, then normalizes empty or inverted ranges to empty. It walks subpages while adjusting offsets across page boundaries, creates at most one temporary mapping per subpage covering either range, zeroes only the intersecting portions, and after unmapping performs cache maintenance per touched subpage before asserting all offsets fully consumed.

Longterm acquisition always requests longterm pinning and optionally adds write permission. Fast selection avoids the address space lock, while the slow path holds it across the whole loop. Benchmark timing reports acquisition and release durations separately in microseconds, reuses the page count to mean actually pinned pages, and rewrites the size field to the number of bytes actually visited.

A single central spin lock guards the count array, the reserved window table and the page association updates for persistent mapping. One build variant disables interrupts around the critical section while another uses plain acquire and release. Callers that may run in atomic context use flag-saving variants. The lock is held across lookup, allocation, count bump, flush and unmap decisions, but released across sleeping waits.

Each page-address hash bucket has its own spin lock held with interrupts saved across list inspection and mutation. The test session mutex serializes longterm start, stop and read against each other and is acquired killably. The address space read lock, when required, is held killably across the entire benchmark or longterm loop and released exactly once on all exit paths that acquired it.

The benchmark loop starts with lock acquisition and allocation, then iterates over the range in chunks bounded by the per-call limit and the range end. Each iteration dispatches on command to a get or pin primitive, stops on error or short return, accumulates the pinned total, and after timing verifies pinned state, optionally dumps, times the release of all pages, unlocks and frees.

Persistent allocation scans for a zero count slot under lock, flushing all singly referenced slots whenever the scan wraps. If a full pass finds no free slot it queues on the shared wait channel, releases the lock, sleeps, then reacquires and rechecks for a concurrent mapping before restarting the scan. On success it installs the table entry, marks the count singly referenced and records the association.

Local mapping disables migration then preemption, pushes the nesting depth, derives the fixed address, fetches the slot table entry, requires it to be empty, installs the new entry, runs a post hook, saves protection state and reenables preemption while keeping migration disabled. Unmapping disables preemption, validates the address against the expected slot, runs a pre hook, clears the entry, runs a post hook, clears saved state, pops the depth and reenables preemption and migration.

Unmapping decrements the slot count under lock. Decrement to zero is fatal, to one records a possible wakeup when waiters exist, and larger values need no further action. Wakeup occurs after unlock. Reverse lookup warns when the address falls in the persistent or local windows yet fails to match, otherwise returns the associated page or falls back to direct conversion.

Overflow, misalignment, unknown commands, empty sizes, oversized longterm ranges, flag bits outside the allowed mask, and starting a second longterm session all fail with invalid argument. User copy faults fail, killable lock acquisition can be interrupted, and short or failed acquisitions terminate the loop early. Misuse such as unbalanced nesting, mapping over a non-empty slot, unmapping the wrong address, dropping a count to zero, or querying a non-high page association triggers fatal or one-time warnings.

Six benchmark and dump commands share read-write direction, magic letter g and numbers one through six, each carrying the main test descriptor. Longterm start uses write direction with number seven carrying the longterm descriptor, stop uses no-data direction with number eight, and read uses write direction with number nine carrying a sixty-four bit destination address.

The dump selection table holds 8 entries. The dump path selects pinning when the lowest test flag bit is set, corresponding to value 1. Longterm write selection uses value 1 and fast selection uses value 2. The local nesting step is 2 in one build configuration and 1 in the other.
The test node is created in the debug filesystem under name gup_test with mode 0600 granting owner read and write only.

Default local hooks for post map and pre or post unmap do nothing, table installation delegates to the generic table update, high-memory fast lookup returns empty, and the persistent-window unmap helper only acts when the architecture requests it, otherwise reporting no action.
